digest.top_line: Chinese phase 3: 54Gy/30fx BID SIB vs 45Gy in LS-SCLC, mOS 60.7 vs 39.5mo (HR 0.55), no added oesophagitis or pneumonitis.
digest.tldr: Thoracic carried the day: hyperfractionated dose escalation delivered as an SIB with involved-field-only volumes finally beat 45Gy BID where CONVERT and CALGB 30610 failed, though early stopping and a 39.5mo control arm both inflate the read. Breast offers two RT-adjacent cautions: tamoxifen's 15yr IBR benefit in good-risk DCIS comes from a non-randomized, imbalanced comparison on the no-RT path, and the proton capsular-contracture signal in PMRT collapses once reconstruction type is modeled.

sites.intro: Both reads are about what happens off the randomized path: an optional-tamoxifen cohort analysis and a retrospective proton-vs-photon PMRT comparison confounded by reconstruction type.

studies.name: NRG/RTOG 9804 + E5194 Combined Analysis
studies.tldr: 15yr IBR 11.4% vs 19.0% with tamoxifen after lumpectomy alone; MVA HR 0.54 (0.35-0.83) for any IBR.
details: 🔍 Ancillary exploratory pooled analysis: non-RT arm of NRG/RTOG 9804 (n=317) + good-risk E5194 cohort (n=561), N=878
🔍 Good-risk definition: low/intermediate grade, ≤2.5 cm, margins ≥3 mm
⚠️ Tamoxifen was OPTIONAL and not randomized in either trial, so this is a non-randomized comparison of a self/physician-selected group

details.text: 📊 Tamoxifen vs no tamoxifen, lumpectomy alone (median f/u 14.85 yrs)

details: 📊 117 IBR events total (65 invasive, 52 DCIS) across 878 pts
⚠️ Tamoxifen uptake differed sharply by trial: 65.6% in 9804 vs 30.3% in E5194, so trial membership tracks exposure

details.text: ⚠️ Baseline imbalances favoring the tamoxifen group
subdetails: More often from NRG/RTOG 9804: 55.0% vs 21.8%, p<0.0001
Negative re-excision more common: 27.2% vs 10.6%, p<0.0001
Pathologic size ≤5 mm more common: 57.0% vs 41.3%, p<0.0001

details: 🔗 The parent 9804 randomization already showed RT lowers IBR in this same good-risk cohort; this analysis speaks only to the no-RT path
⚠️ ER status not reported in source text, so the endocrine-sensitive denominator for this effect is undefined here

verdict.rationale: Non-randomized tamoxifen use pooled across two trials, exploratory ancillary analysis, with baseline imbalances (re-excision, size ≤5 mm) that independently favor the tamoxifen group.
verdict.audience: Good-risk DCIS post-lumpectomy without RT, low/int grade, ≤2.5 cm, margins ≥3 mm

studies.significance: For the RT-omission conversation this quantifies the alternative: 15-yr IBR 19.0% without either modality, 11.4% with tamoxifen alone. Note the invasive/DCIS split, invasive IBR HR 0.43 (0.24-0.77) but DCIS-IBR p=0.089, so the benefit falls on the event type that drives salvage mastectomy and systemic risk.
studies.monday_clinic: In good-risk DCIS (low/intermediate grade, ≤2.5 cm, margins ≥3 mm) who has already declined RT after lumpectomy, this supports discussing endocrine therapy as the remaining risk-reduction option; it does not inform whether tamoxifen substitutes for RT, since no randomized RT-vs-tamoxifen comparison exists here.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: **Ancillary exploratory** combined analysis of two cooperative-group trials, pooling the **non-RT arm of NRG/RTOG 9804** with the **good-risk cohort of E5194**. Tamoxifen use was **optional, not randomized**, in both. Fine-Gray univariate and multivariable competing-risk regression.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: N=**878** (317 from NRG/RTOG 9804, 561 from E5194). Good-risk DCIS defined as **low or intermediate grade, ≤2.5 cm, excision margins ≥3 mm**. Median age 59 (28-88). Tamoxifen use **43.1%** overall.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: IBR, invasive-IBR, DCIS-IBR, contralateral breast event, and overall survival, compared between tamoxifen-use groups. No single registered primary endpoint is stated for this ancillary analysis.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: At median follow-up **14.85 years**, 117 IBR (65 invasive, 52 DCIS). Effect sizes are in the table above. The separation is on **invasive** recurrence, not DCIS recurrence.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents good-risk DCIS (low/intermediate grade, ≤2.5 cm, margins ≥3 mm) treated with lumpectomy alone and no RT. Does not represent high-grade or larger DCIS, close margins, or pts who received adjuvant RT.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Beyond the non-randomized exposure: tamoxifen **duration, adherence and ER status are not reported in the source text**, and the two trials contribute unequally (65.6% vs 30.3% uptake), so trial-era effects and tamoxifen exposure are partly collinear. Contralateral breast event and OS results are listed in Table 2 but not given numerically in the source text.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: This sizes the counterfactual you quote when a good-risk DCIS pt declines RT: 15-yr IBR 19.0% with lumpectomy alone versus 11.4% with tamoxifen. The benefit is concentrated in invasive IBR (HR 0.43, 0.24-0.77) with DCIS-IBR non-significant (p=0.089), which matters because invasive recurrence is what carries salvage and systemic consequences. It does not license substituting tamoxifen for RT, no randomized comparison here.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Fifteen-year absolute IBR difference is 7.6 points (19.0% to 11.4%) in a good-risk, lumpectomy-only DCIS population, with the effect on invasive IBR (HR 0.43) rather than DCIS-IBR (p=0.089). ER status, tamoxifen duration and adherence are not reported in source text, so the denominator for endocrine sensitivity and the required exposure remain undefined for a counseling conversation.

Whether aromatase inhibitors give the same IBR reduction in this cohort

studies.name: Pencil Beam Scanning Proton vs IMRT PMRT: Capsular Contracture
studies.tldr: 2yr capsular contracture 50% with proton+DTI vs 12% photon+TE/I; proton effect lost significance on multivariable (HR 1.76, P=.083).
details: 📐 Proton vs photon CC on univariate: HR 2.3 (95% CI 1.26-4.30), P=.007
⚠️ Signal did not survive adjustment: MVA HR 1.76 (0.93-3.32), P=.083
📊 Reconstruction type dominated the model: DTI vs TE/I HR 3.0 (1.7-5.5), P<.001

details.text: 📊 2yr CC rate by modality × reconstruction type (P<.001)

details: 🔍 Retrospective cohort, 2 centers in one institution, N=175 (89 proton, 86 photon), 2017-2023
🔍 All reconstructions subpectoral; every TE/I patient had the expander irradiated
⚠️ Arms imbalanced on reconstruction type (P<.001) and tumor laterality (P<.001)
🔍 Median f/u 42mo proton vs 47mo photon; median age 49, 63% Hispanic
⚠️ No RT dose, fractionation, or skin/chest wall dose reported in source abstract

verdict.rationale: Retrospective, and the arms were imbalanced on reconstruction type, the variable that dominated the model; the proton association did not survive multivariable adjustment (P=.083).
verdict.audience: Breast cancer, subpectoral implant reconstruction, receiving PMRT

studies.significance: The decision this moves is reconstruction pairing, not beam choice: DTI carried HR 3.0 for CC independent of modality, and proton+DTI reached 50% 2yr CC vs 12% for photon+TE/I. Where protons are chosen for cardiac sparing, staged TE/I was the lower-CC pairing here.
studies.monday_clinic: In a pt where proton PMRT is on the table for cardiac and pulmonary sparing, this informs the implant reconstruction choice (staged TE/I vs DTI) more than the beam choice; it does not extend to prepectoral or autologous reconstruction, which this cohort excluded.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: IRB-approved **retrospective** cohort across **2 centers within a single institution**, Jan 2017 to Dec 2023, **N=175** (89 proton, 86 photon). CC estimated by Kaplan-Meier, with Cox proportional hazards and a binary logistic model as verification.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Breast cancer pts after **subpectoral** 2-stage tissue expander/implant or **direct-to-implant** reconstruction. Median age **49** (24-78), **63% Hispanic**. Groups were balanced except **tumor laterality** (P<.001) and **reconstruction type** (P<.001).

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **Pencil beam scanning proton** PMRT vs **IMRT photon** PMRT. All TE/I pts had the **expander irradiated**. Dose, fractionation, and skin or chest wall dose constraints are not reported in the source abstract, so plan comparability cannot be assessed.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: Capsular contracture was the outcome; no registered primary endpoint is stated. Median follow-up **42 mo** (proton) and **47 mo** (photon).

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: The proton association was significant on univariate analysis but **not** on multivariable (**P=.083**), while reconstruction type held (**DTI HR 3.0**). No other variable was associated with CC.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents subpectoral implant-based reconstruction receiving proton or photon PMRT at a proton-capable center, median age 49 and majority Hispanic. Does not represent prepectoral placement, autologous reconstruction, or pts receiving PMRT without reconstruction.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The **photon DTI cell holds 15 pts**, so the thinnest cell anchors the headline contrast. Reconstruction type is both the strongest predictor and the variable the arms differed on, so modality and reconstruction choice are confounded by referral pattern. No CC grading scale or dosimetry reported.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The abstract's own framing is that protons improve cardiac and pulmonary dosimetry; this cohort prices that gain in implant morbidity rather than in survival. The read is a trade to discuss at consult, not a reason to withhold protons.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The proton CC signal did not survive adjustment (HR 1.76, P=.083), so beam choice is not the lever; reconstruction is. Where protons are used for cardiac and pulmonary sparing, proton+DTI ran 50% 2yr CC vs 23% for proton+TE/I, which is the pairing worth flagging at simulation.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: DTI was the dominant predictor on multivariable analysis (HR 3.0, 1.7-5.5, P<.001), independent of beam. With PMRT planned, staged TE/I ran 23% (proton) and 12% (photon) 2yr CC vs 50% and 35% for DTI, informing the reconstruction technique conversation before RT starts.

sites.intro: First positive high-dose LS-SCLC trial to keep the BID schedule, and it escalates the GTV alone while holding the PTV at 45Gy.

studies.name: High-Dose Hyperfractionated SIB RT vs Standard-Dose RT for LS-SCLC
studies.tldr: mOS 60.7 vs 39.5mo, HR 0.55 (0.37-0.72), p=0.003 with 54Gy/30fx BID SIB vs 45Gy, no added toxicity.
details: 🔍 Open-label phase 3, 16 Chinese hospitals, N=224, 1:1, ITT primary; stopped early Apr 2021 by DSMB for benefit
🔍 Dose delivered as SIB: GTV/IGTV to 54Gy, PTV held at 45Gy in BOTH arms · 30 fx BID, ≥6h apart, 10 fx/wk over 3 wks
🔍 Involved-field only: GTV = primary + PET-CT-positive nodes, CTV = GTV + 5mm; elective nodal irradiation omitted; VMAT, 4DCT, CBCT
🔍 Concurrent cis/carbo + etoposide, 4 cycles in 99% of pts; PCI 25Gy/10fx in 82% vs 81%
📊 Efficacy, 54Gy vs 45Gy (median f/u 46mo)

details.text: 📊 RT-attributable toxicity, no separation between arms
subdetails: Late G3 pneumonitis 2 (2%) vs 3 (3%); no late G3 oesophagitis or stricture in either arm
One treatment-related death in the 54Gy arm (myocardial infarction)

details: 📊 First-relapse sites similar: total 59 (55%) vs 65 (56%), p=0.494; chest 32 (30%) vs 36 (31%), brain 14 (13%) vs 13 (11%)
🔗 vs CONVERT (66Gy QD) and CALGB 30610 (70Gy QD): both failed to beat 45Gy BID · neither high-dose arm was hyperfractionated or accelerated
🔗 vs the Nordic phase 2 (60Gy/40fx BID): 2-yr OS 74.2% vs 48.1%, same direction and similar magnitude
⚠️ Terminated early at interim after 88 deaths (HR 0.50) of a planned 326 pts / 176 events; early stopping inflates the effect estimate
⚠️ Control arm mOS 39.5mo far exceeds the 24mo planning assumption and prior 45Gy series (20.8-30mo), so the population is selected
⚠️ Age >70 and ECOG 2 excluded; median LS-SCLC age is 67 in NCDB, so the trial cohort is younger than the clinic
⚠️ No central QA, open-label, single-country; GTV/PTV volumes not controlled for in stratification

verdict.rationale: Randomised phase 3, prespecified OS primary hit at interim. Offers a BID dose-escalation route where CONVERT and CALGB 30610 once-daily escalation failed. Early stopping caveat.
verdict.audience: LS-SCLC, age 18-70, ECOG 0-1, PET-CT staged, stage II-III

studies.significance: The escalation is SIB-only: GTV to 54Gy while PTV stayed at 45Gy in both arms, with involved-field targeting off PET-CT and no elective nodal irradiation. That is why oesophagitis (13% vs 12%) did not move, and it is the specific plan a reader would have to reproduce for the 21.2-month OS gain to transfer.
studies.monday_clinic: In a PET-staged LS-SCLC patient aged 70 or under with ECOG 0-1 starting concurrent chemoRT, this supports a 54Gy SIB to GTV within a 45Gy PTV over flat 45Gy BID; it does not extend to older or ECOG 2 pts, who were excluded.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Open-label randomised **phase 3** at **16 public hospitals in China**, 1:1, enrolled Jun 2017 to Apr 2021. Stratified by ECOG, stage, prior chemo course and platinum choice. Median follow-up **46 months** (IQR 33-56); **terminated early** by the DSMB in Apr 2021 for benefit.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: **Aged 18-70**, ECOG **0-1**, LS-SCLC by Veterans Administration staging with **mandatory whole-body FDG PET-CT and brain MRI**. N=224 (108 vs 116); median age 64, 46% female, 86% stage III. ECOG 2 and age >70 excluded.

analysis_sections.label: Regimen
analysis_sections.body: Four cycles of **cisplatin 75 mg/m² or carboplatin AUC 5 plus etoposide 100 mg/m² d1-3**, concurrent with thoracic RT started 0-42 days after cycle 1. **99%** completed four cycles in both arms. PCI 25Gy/10fx given to 82% vs 81%.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: VMAT, **30 fractions twice daily**, minimum 6h interfraction, 10 fx/week over 3 weeks. Experimental arm used a **simultaneous integrated boost: 54Gy to GTV/IGTV with the PTV held at 45Gy**; control arm 45Gy to both. GTV was primary tumour plus **PET-CT-positive nodes only, elective nodal irradiation omitted**, CTV = GTV + 5mm.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: **Primary: overall survival** in the ITT population, timed from start of chemotherapy. Secondary: PFS, local PFS, metastatic-free survival, disease control rate, acute and late toxicity, HRQOL (reported elsewhere).

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: OS, PFS and local PFS all favoured 54Gy; metastasis-free survival did not separate. Disease control rate 97% vs 93%, p=0.218. See the efficacy table.

analysis_sections.label: Safety
analysis_sections.body: No signal of added toxicity from the boost. Grade 3-4 neutropenia **44% vs 41%** (p=0.64), thrombocytopenia 13% vs 14%, anaemia 9% vs 8%. Severe acute oesophagitis stayed **below 15%**, well under the 32% reported with elective nodal irradiation in Intergroup 0096.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Once-daily escalation failed twice: **CONVERT** 66Gy gave mOS 25 vs 30 months and **CALGB 30610/RTOG 0538** 70Gy gave 28.5 vs 30.1 months against 45Gy BID. The Nordic randomised phase 2 escalating **within** the BID schedule (60Gy/40fx) raised 2-year OS to **74.2% vs 48.1%**, matching the direction here.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents PET-staged, ECOG 0-1 LS-SCLC pts aged 70 or under treated with involved-field VMAT and concurrent platinum-etoposide. Does not represent pts over 70, ECOG 2, or programmes that cannot deliver twice-daily fractionation.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: The control arm's **39.5-month** mOS exceeds every published 45Gy BID series (20.8-30 months) and the trial's own 24-month planning assumption, so the cohort is favourably selected and the absolute gain may not port. **No centralised QA**, and total tumour and RT volumes were not balanced by stratification.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: This is a boost question, not a whole-field dose question: GTV took 54Gy while the PTV stayed at 45Gy in both arms, delivered BID over 3 weeks with involved-field PET-based targeting and no elective nodal irradiation. Acute G3-4 oesophagitis held at 13% vs 12%, which is what makes the plan reproducible.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: The systemic backbone was identical (4 cycles platinum-etoposide in 99% of pts, PCI in ~82%), so the 21.2-month OS gain is attributable to the RT dose, not the regimen. Haematologic G3-4 toxicity did not rise (neutropenia 44% vs 41%), so referring for BID escalation costs nothing on the chemo side.

papers.title: Impact of Tamoxifen Only After Lumpectomy for "Good-Risk" Duct Carcinoma In Situ: Combined Analysis of the NRG Oncology/RTOG 9804 and ECOG-ACRIN E5194 Trials.
papers.journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
papers.abstract:
PURPOSE: The NRG Oncology/Radiation Therapy Oncology Group (RTOG) 9804 trial randomized patients with "good-risk" ductal carcinoma in situ (DCIS) to radiation (RT) or no RT following lumpectomy. The Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group-American College of Radiology Imaging Network E5194 trial had a comparable cohort observed without RT. Tamoxifen use was optional in both trials. This ancillary exploratory analysis combining both data sets assessed the effect of tamoxifen on ipsilateral breast recurrence (IBR) in "good-risk" DCIS treated with lumpectomy alone.

METHODS AND MATERIALS: A combined database from the non-RT arm of NRG/RTOG 9804 and the "good-risk" cohort from E5194 (low- or intermediate-grade, ≤2.5 cm, excision margins ≥3 mm) was created, and distributions of patient and DCIS characteristics by tamoxifen use were compared by χ2. IBR, invasive IBR, DCIS-IBR, contralateral breast event, and overall survival were estimated, and distributions were compared between tamoxifen use groups. Univariate and multivariable Fine-Gray regression models were used to analyze factors that may be associated with endpoints.

RESULTS: Eight hundred and seventy-eight patients were analyzed (317 from NRG/RTOG 9804 and 561 from E5194). The use of tamoxifen overall was 43.1% (65.6% in NRG/RTOG 9804 and 30.3% in E5194). At a median follow-up of 14.85 years, there were 117 IBRs (65 invasive and 52 DCIS). There was a significant association for reduced IBR with tamoxifen use (P = .001); estimated 15-year IBR with tamoxifen is 11.4% (95% CI, 7.9-15.5) and without is 19.0% (15.3-22.9). Tamoxifen use was significantly associated with reduced invasive IBR (P = .0048) but not DCIS-IBR (P = .089). On multivariable analysis, patients who received tamoxifen were 46% less likely to have any IBR (hazard ratio, 0.54; 95% CI, 0.35-0.83; P = .0045), and 57% less likely to have invasive IBR (hazard ratio, 0.43; 95% CI, 0.24-0.77; P = 0.0042).

CONCLUSION: For patients with "good-risk" DCIS treated with lumpectomy without RT, tamoxifen use was significantly associated with a reduction in IBR overall and invasive IBR, not DCIS-IBR.

papers.title: Does Pencil Beam Scanning Proton Therapy Impart a Higher Risk of Capsular Contracture Compared With Intensity Modulated Photon Radiation Therapy in the Postmastectomy Reconstruction Setting?
papers.journal: International journal of radiation oncology, biology, physics
papers.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postmastectomy radiation therapy (PMRT) may cause adverse events in the reconstruction setting. Proton-based PMRT is increasingly used and has been shown to improve cardiac and pulmonary dosimetry. Data on the risk of capsular contracture (CC) with proton versus photon PMRT remain scarce. We compared the CC rate of the largest cohort of patients undergoing reconstruction after pencil beam scanning proton PMRT reported to date with an intensity modulated radiation therapy photon cohort, hypothesizing that the proton cohort would have a higher rate of CC.

METHODS AND MATERIALS: An institutional review board -approved retrospective study was conducted on patients with breast cancer who underwent subpectoral 2-stage tissue expander/implant (TE/I) or direct-to-implant (DTI) breast reconstruction and received either pencil beam scanning proton or intensity modulated radiation therapy photon PMRT between January 2017 and December 2023 at 2 centers within a single institution. All patients undergoing TE/I had the TE irradiated. CC rates were estimated using the Kaplan-Meier method. Cox proportional hazards analysis, denoted as hazard ratios (HRs) with 95% CIs, was used to assess variables potentially associated with the outcome, and a binary logistic regression model was used to verify the results.

RESULTS: The study cohort comprised 175 patients (89 proton; 86 photon). The median age was 49 years (range, 24-78), 63% were Hispanic. Patient demographics were well balanced between the groups, except in tumor laterality (P < .001) and reconstruction type (TE/I vs DTI; P < .001). The median follow-up was 42 and 47 months for the proton and photon groups, respectively. In a multivariable analysis, DTI patients had a significantly higher risk of CC compared with TE/I patients (HR, 3.0; 95% CI, 1.7-5.5; P < .001). Proton patients had a higher risk of developing CC compared with the photon group in univariate analysis (HR, 2.3; 95% CI, 1.26-4.30; P = .007), although this effect did not reach statistical significance in the multivariable model (HR, 1.76; 95% CI, 0.93-3.32; P = .083). The 2-year CC rate for patients treated with protons and DTI (n = 36), photons and DTI (n = 15), protons and TE/I (n = 53), and photons and TE/I (n = 71) was 50%, 35%, 23%, 12%, respectively (P < .001). No other factors were significantly associated with CC development.

CONCLUSION: In this contemporary large proton versus photon PMRT cohort, patients treated with proton showed a trend toward an increased risk of CC. Patients undergoing DTI who were treated with protons had the highest risk of CC (50%). Careful consideration of reconstruction and radiation therapy modalities, assessing CC risk, and also involving patient input, is important for treatment selection.
